questions: Should the function count escaped bracket characters in string representations (e.g., '\(') as a bracket, or only literal bracket characters?
If a cell contains a non-string type (e.g., integer, float, None, NaN), does str(x) produce a representation that might contain brackets (e.g., 'nan' or '(1+2j)') that should be counted?
Does the pattern '[(){}[\]]' match a backslash character '\' as a bracket, since the pattern includes an escaped ']'?
Should overlapping bracket matches be counted? For example, in '[[', does re.findall count two '[' or one match of '[' and then another?
If the DataFrame has a MultiIndex or special column/row labels containing brackets, should those be included in the count?
Should the function handle nested DataFrames or Series within cells (e.g., a cell containing another DataFrame)?
Is the function case-sensitive regarding bracket characters? (It is, but confirmation needed for non-standard brackets like full-width brackets?)
Should the count include brackets that appear as part of a larger Unicode character or combined grapheme?
